# Metaplate v0.8.1

Metaplate 0.8.1 closes the gaps found by putting 0.8.0 into production on a real Next.js static export. Three new render guards catch text that sits in a crop strip, crowds other text, or runs under a photo. `--require-content` now checks JPEG cards. `verify` takes directories and globs, so it works in npm scripts on Windows, and `runCli` runs any command from a script without a shell. `verify-page` reads the `twitter:image` type and size that Next.js emits, and stops warning about formats it has already measured.

> **Upgrade recommendation:** Recommended for every 0.8.0 user. The `satori` peer floor rises to 0.38.2: if your project pins an older Satori, upgrade it first (see [Breaking changes](#breaking-changes)).

## Why upgrade

- **Catch broken cards that stay inside the canvas.** `overflow` only sees text that leaves the image. The new `safeArea`, `textOverlap`, and `avoid` guards fail a footer pushed into the strip X's 2:1 crop removes, a line crowding the one below it, and a headline running under a photo.
- **Check JPEG cards after the build.** The rendering guide recommends JPEG for photographic cards, and `--require-content` now decodes JPEG as well as PNG, so a blank JPEG card fails the build.
- **See what a dependency upgrade changed.** Guards say nothing is broken, not that nothing moved. `metaplate verify --baseline` compares every card with a saved copy and fails the ones that changed, with a picture of each change, so a Satori, Resvg, or font upgrade cannot quietly shift every card.
- **Verify every card from any shell, or from code.** `metaplate verify out/og` and `metaplate verify "out/og/*/og-image.jpg"` work in npm scripts on Windows, where `cmd.exe` expands nothing. `runCli` from `metaplate/cli` runs the same commands in-process.

## Highlights

### Render guards

- **`safeArea`** reports text outside the area that the centered 2:1 crop (X `summary_large_image`) and the 1.91:1 crop (Open Graph) both keep. For 1200x630 that removes 15px from the top and bottom, the same crops `metaplate preview` overlays. `{ level, inset }` sets your own margin instead.
- **`textOverlap`** reports two text elements whose boxes intersect.
- **`avoid: { level, keys, gap }`** reports text within `gap` pixels of an element whose React `key` is listed, such as `key="photo"` on an `<img>`.
- All three run in `createSvgOg`, `createNodeOg`, and `createEdgeOg`, and each issue lists the text and its box. See [Render guards](https://github.com/lnorton89/metaplate/blob/v0.8.1/docs/rendering.md#render-guards).
- `metaplate/node` and `metaplate/edge` now export the `SatoriOptions` and `SatoriLayoutNode` types, so `satori: { onNodeDetected }` no longer needs a cast to Satori's own `SatoriOptions`, which requires `width`, `height`, and `fonts`.

### Image and page checks

- **`verify --baseline DIR` compares cards with a baseline.** Each PNG or JPEG is matched with the file at the same relative path in `DIR`. A card fails when more of its pixels changed than `--max-diff` allows (default 0), when it has no baseline, or when a baseline file has no card. `--threshold` sets how far a channel may move before a pixel counts as changed: 0 for PNG by default, and 16 when either side is a JPEG, so re-encoding noise does not count. `--write-diff DIR` writes the baseline, the current card, and the changed pixels in red side by side, and `--update-baseline` rewrites the baseline after review. `compareImages` from `metaplate/node` runs the same comparison in tests. JPEGs are fully decoded with no new dependency, within a few levels of libjpeg. See [Compare against a baseline](https://github.com/lnorton89/metaplate/blob/v0.8.1/docs/verification.md#compare-against-a-baseline).
- **`--require-content` decodes JPEG.** Baseline and progressive Huffman JPEGs are supported, with any chroma subsampling, restart markers, grayscale, and Adobe CMYK, and no new dependency. A JPEG fails only when every 8x8 block of every channel holds the same flat value, so a card with any detail never fails. WebP and GIF still fail with the flag, and that error now points to the plate's `guards: { blank: "error" }`. See [Require visible content](https://github.com/lnorton89/metaplate/blob/v0.8.1/docs/verification.md#require-visible-content).
- **`verify` takes directories and globs.** A directory stands for every image file below it (limited to `--format` when given). Globs support `*`, `?`, `**`, `[...]`, and `{a,b}`. Files are checked in sorted order, once each. See [Directories and globs](https://github.com/lnorton89/metaplate/blob/v0.8.1/docs/verification.md#directories-and-globs).
- **`metaplate/cli` (new entry)** exports `runCli(args, { stdout, stderr })`. It resolves to the exit code, leaves `process.exitCode` alone, and keeps concurrent calls apart. See [Run the CLI from a script](https://github.com/lnorton89/metaplate/blob/v0.8.1/docs/verification.md#run-the-cli-from-a-script).
- **`verify-page` reads `twitter:image:type`, `:width`, and `:height`.** [Next.js metadata](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) emits them for a JPEG plate, and they are now checked against the fetched bytes like the `og:image:*` properties. When a page declares no type, target format rules read the fetched bytes instead of warning that compatibility "cannot be confirmed". See [Page audits](https://github.com/lnorton89/metaplate/blob/v0.8.1/docs/verify-page.md).

## Breaking changes

- **The `satori` peer range is now `>=0.38.2 <1`** (was `>=0.33.3 <1`). Releases below 0.38.2 drop content without an error, and no guard can see it:
  - before 0.38.2, `inset` is ignored, so an `inset: 0` overlay collapses to 0x0;
  - through 0.35.1, `color: "transparent"` text, the usual way to draw outline type with `WebkitTextStroke`, draws nothing;
  - 0.35.2 to 0.37.0 fail on import under Node ESM;
  - before 0.38.2, a fragment is laid out as a box of its own.

  Each was checked on Satori 0.33.5 through 0.63.2. This is a peer contract change in a patch release; a project on an older Satori gets a peer-dependency warning (or an `ERESOLVE` error under strict peers) until it upgrades.
- **`verify-page` target format results change for undeclared types.** A page with no `og:image:type` now passes `universal` when the fetched image is PNG or JPEG (it was an error), and `x` now fails an undeclared SVG (it was a warning). `socialImageCompatibility` and `verifySocialImage` are unchanged.

Upgrade advice: run `npm install satori@0.63` if `npm ls satori` shows a release below 0.38.2. Then re-run your `verify-page --target` checks once.

## Install or upgrade

```sh
npm install metaplate@0.8.1
```

That single command still includes the framework-neutral SVG and PNG renderer: npm 7+ and pnpm 8+ install the `satori`, `@resvg/resvg-js`, and `react` peers. Yarn needs them added explicitly. Node.js 20 or newer is required.

Peer changes: `satori` rises to `>=0.38.2 <1` (audited release 0.63.2). `@resvg/resvg-wasm` and `next` stay optional and unchanged.

New entry point: `metaplate/cli`.

## Verification

- `npm run check` passes: lint, the duplication scan, workflow pin policy, dependency inventory and Socket disposition policy, deployment evidence policy, release-note validation, source and example type checks, 1,318 tests, the build, and the package dry run.
- `npm run check:package` installs the exact local tarball into clean consumers and builds, serves, and fetches images from every framework fixture.
- The full JPEG decode behind `--baseline` was compared with libjpeg (Pillow) on baseline 4:2:0, progressive 4:2:2, 4:4:4, and grayscale images: every channel of every pixel was within 4 levels, and the test suite checks two of those against libjpeg's own output.
- The JPEG content check was compared with libjpeg (Pillow) on 400 random JPEGs: baseline and progressive, every chroma subsampling, grayscale, CMYK, and restart intervals, flat and with one changed pixel. It agreed on every file.
- **Socket baseline.** It is the Socket CLI deep score of the published `metaplate@0.8.0`, captured 2026-11-03. The package scores 78 overall; its own alerts are `recentlyPublished` (medium) and `urlStrings` (low). The same two high dependency alerts as 0.8.0 carry time-bounded dispositions that expire 2027-04-30: `string.prototype.codepointat`, under the Satori peer, and `tslib@2.9.1`'s ownership change, reached only through optional and development dependencies. Socket scores only published packages, so 0.8.1 is scored after publication.
- **Hosted deployments.** After publication, the Vercel, Netlify, and Deno Deploy fixtures are redeployed with the published 0.8.1 and checked for status, media type, dimensions, response headers, distinct bytes per slug, and non-blank content. That evidence is recorded in [`.planning/hosted-evidence/`](https://github.com/lnorton89/metaplate/tree/main/.planning/hosted-evidence).
- npm registry signature and SLSA provenance verification run after publication, against the published artifact.
